direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a pure Node.js ESM migration with .mjs modules, manual argv parsing, bidict behavior, no external dependencies, and output under /output.
Parallel cell metadata records actual parallel use, four subagents, successful artifact copy, and official failure at 57 of 70 tests.
Current completed official evaluation is the source of truth and reports solution_passed false with 57/70 samples passed.
Evaluation summary confirms the official RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed, succeeded operationally, and marked the solution failed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event journal mirrors the main session lifecycle from prompt start through completed turn and contains only transport-level projection entries.
Session index identifies the parallel session directory and workspace path for the raw actor trajectories.
Subagent agent-0 owned /output/lib/pyformat.mjs, wrote Python repr formatting helpers, ran syntax and ad hoc ESM checks, probed reference output, and returned a complete summary.
Subagent agent-1 owned /output/lib/bidict.mjs, wrote the bidict class and error types, ran syntax and semantic harnesses, cleaned temporary test state, and returned its contract.
Subagent agent-2 owned /output/lib/argparse.mjs, extensively probed argparse behavior, wrote the parser, ran 53 differential cases, removed the temporary harness, and returned details.
Subagent agent-3 owned /output/test8.mjs, probed traceback behavior, wrote the entry point, ran node --check, and noted full end-to-end testing depended on sibling modules.

The parallel parent probed the executable, delegated four explicit module scopes through AgentSwarm, received all child results, ran integrated differential checks, inspected final files, and delivered.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same ESM, argv, formatting, no-dependency, and /output deliverable constraints.
Serial cell metadata records no parallel use, no subagents, successful artifact copy, and official failure at 57 of 70 tests.
Current completed official evaluation is the source of truth and reports solution_passed false with 57/70 samples passed.
Evaluation summary confirms the official RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed, succeeded operationally, and marked the serial solution failed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event journal mirrors the serial session lifecycle from prompt start through completed turn and contains only transport-level projection entries.
Session index identifies the serial session directory and workspace path for the raw main-agent trajectory.
The serial main agent probed behavior, wrote all modules itself, renamed an internal Map-like helper, verified samples and edge cases, patched duplicate-value handling, and delivered.

parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output, manual command-line parsing, bidict behavior, Python repr formatting, no external dependencies, and /output placement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent probed executable behavior, then assigned four distinct file/module owners through AgentSwarm and kept parent responsibility for final integration and verification.
parallel.implementation: Subagents produced pyformat, bidict, argparse, and test8 entry modules with explicit contracts; argparse and formatting were probed deeply and entry handled traceback-like failures.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent received all child summaries, ran integrated differential testing against the reference executable, normalized the help-name diff, listed final /output, read files, and delivered code.
parallel.verification: Children ran local syntax or module harnesses, and parent ran a multi-case end-to-end differential harness before the official evaluator later scored 57/70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished child or unjoined result is visible; hidden official failures remain, but the pair data exposes only aggregate 57/70 rather than the exact missed cases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs output, manual parser, bidict representation, no dependencies, and generated library plus entry files under /output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single main agent owned the complete pipeline: probing, writing modules, editing fixes, testing, and final delivery with no subagents.
serial.implementation: Wrote pyrepr, bidict, argparse, and test8 modules directly, then renamed an internal Map-like helper and patched duplicate-value behavior after inspecting bidict code.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All artifacts were generated by the serial main agent and were tested from /output before final response.
serial.verification: Ran sample-case diffs, equals-form and negative-value checks, missing/invalid argument checks, and duplicate-value exit-code checks before official 57/70 evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No incomplete work is visible; like parallel, official hidden failures remain unresolved in the available pair-local evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the ESM, no-dependency, manual parsing, bidict behavior, repr formatting, and /output requirements before delegating modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and implemented ESM modules, manual parsing, bidict behavior, and output files under /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap is visible; parallel documented more edge behavior, while both satisfied the visible structural requirements and both still failed hidden evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into four owned files and made the parent the integrator after subagent completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification ownership in the main agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit module ownership boundaries; serial had no coordination boundary but a single owner for all modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated with shared contracts for ESM, file paths, BigInt values, no Map, and module exports, then received child handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial controlled interfaces locally among its own pyrepr, bidict, argparse, and entry modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent interface risk but the handoffs and final imports were compatible; serial avoided cross-agent interface transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a detailed argparse replica, bidict implementation, Python repr formatter, and traceback-aware entry point through separate child modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote simpler direct modules, then patched bidict duplicate-value behavior during local review.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel invested more in edge-case emulation through specialized children; serial implemented the whole path directly and fixed one visible gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned through the AgentSwarm result before the parent resumed integration and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local edits and tests stayed in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit join point that completed; serial did not need to retrieve delegated results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files and the parent verified the final /output tree; no same-file overwrite or incompatible final tree is visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial edited its own generated files and reran final checks after the bidict patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared /output across children but with distinct file ownership; serial had one writer, so no inter-agent shared-state hazard existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child-local checks plus parent-level integrated differential tests; official evaluation later completed at 57/70 and failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample and edge-case local checks; official evaluation likewise completed at 57/70 and failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verified more argparse and module edge cases, but neither run reached full official pass and no pair-local per-case failure log explains the remaining 13 failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and much more agent time but finished normally without timeout, then delivered after integrated checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished normally in a shorter single-agent run and delivered after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordination increased elapsed work but did not produce a timeout, cancellation, or unfinished closure; both closed before official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both modes failed the current completed official evaluation with the same 57/70 aggregate. Parallel's delegated implementation and serial's direct implementation differ in organization and edge-case detail, but the available pair-local evidence does not show a coordination failure that explains an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel created specialized module owners and then joined all four results before final integrated verification.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all work in one trajectory and patched a visible bidict duplicate-value issue before final verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented richer argparse and traceback emulation; serial implemented a simpler direct migration. Neither difference changed the official aggregate result.
The official pair data exposes aggregate pass counts but not the hidden per-case failures, so the exact remaining implementation defect is not identified from allowed inputs.

candidates.reason: Implementation owners were explicit: each child owned a concrete output file and wrote it.
The parent owned integration after AgentSwarm returned and ran integrated differential checks.
The entry file had an assigned child owner and the parent confirmed the final /output tree.
The parent controlled probing, delegation, join, integrated testing, and final delivery.
Parent probing preceded delegation but did not block productive work long enough to create an unfinished or shortened implementation consequence.
The parallel run moved from initial probes into overlapping module implementation and completed integration, not a harmful investigation-only phase.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; all module paths completed and parent verified the assembled result.
Four-way fan-out increased work but did not exhaust the run budget or prevent join, verification, or delivery.
No child received an overbroad assignment that remained unfinished; each child returned its owned module.
The child briefs carried the known ESM, no-dependency, output path, BigInt, no-Map, and verification expectations; no unusable child work followed from a missing known requirement.
Separate modules were delegated with explicit file paths and export/import contracts, and the final integrated run did not show incompatible component interfaces.
No known finding is shown disappearing between actors; the parent received and used the child result summaries.
The AgentSwarm handoff was long but the parent consumed it, resumed testing, inspected files, and delivered.
No child report described a superseded workspace state that the parent then acted on incorrectly.
The returned module summaries were compatible enough for imports and integrated tests; no unresolved conflicting contract is visible.
The parent made a final completion statement only after integrated differential checks; the official hidden failure alone is not a parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap.
There was no replacement or retry child that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints.

Verifier findings were not trapped below the parent; child and parent test results were visible in the main trajectory.
No required child failed or was cancelled, so there was no failed child scope needing takeover.
The parent did not ignore a completed child result; it resumed with the returned modules and ran integration checks.
The run did not time out or wait blindly near deadline; the parent acted after the swarm returned.
Children wrote different files with non-overlapping ownership and no competing designs requiring reconciliation are visible.
No two live agents edited the same source file or observed a same-file concurrent change.
No non-entry library or module source owned by another agent was replaced wholesale.
The required entry deliverable had a single child owner and no replacement by another live actor is shown.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated provenance.
Although children wrote in shared /output, ownership was separated by file and no unstable-state or provenance consequence occurred.
Temporary harnesses and probes were used by their own actors and removed or kept outside the deliverable; no concurrent actor consumed leaked artifacts as stable input.
